main_result.result: Superseded the historical launch gate's legacy numerical-replay dependency for new ADMITs. The new gate prepares and acknowledges ADMIT from reservation-compliance replay while retaining the historical ADMIT/SLOT wire format and score-wrapper-facing per-slot gate API. Per-slot freshness uses exact durable ADMIT-prefix and current raw active-ADMIT identity rather than reinterpreting historical numerical rows.

two_block_lifecycle.block1: Three planned slots; two reservation-bound compliant scores of 0 and one physically present favorable lower-level slot with no reservation/binding/commit. Raw physical block score was 0, but compliance scientific score was 1/3 with one fail-closed slot.
two_block_lifecycle.restart1: Compliance replay recovered one reporting row; historical legacy reporting replay conflicted because the audited row intentionally differed from the raw row.
two_block_lifecycle.block2: The migrated gate admitted the next block from compliance-replayed reporter state. A stale block-1 capability was rejected. Two compliant block-2 slots produced scientific score 1/2.
two_block_lifecycle.restart2: Exactly two scientific rows replayed, and a second full replay produced the identical final digest.

measurement_validity_rules: A compliance CLOSE can intentionally make scientific numerical state differ from the raw lower-level SLOT summary; therefore legacy numerical replay cannot be the recovery authority for a subsequent ADMIT.

The next ADMIT must derive its reporting admission from compliance replay over the exact durable main journal plus reservation ledger, while preserving the established ADMIT wire format so historical evidence remains replayable.

After a capability has been issued by compliance-aware replay, per-slot freshness does not need to rerun historical numerical semantics. Exact acknowledged prefix integrity plus current raw active-ADMIT identity, slot plan and deadline are sufficient for this launch-liveness check; reservation/binding/COMMIT compliance remains a separate scientific evidence gate.
Stale capability rejection must include active ADMIT identity/content, not merely block id, to prevent accidental authority reuse if identifiers are recycled.
A physically accepted but reservation-noncompliant slot remains fail-closed in the scientific row even though it can remain in the immutable raw journal.

The launch capability does not bind the whole reservation-ledger prefix after admission because legitimate RESERVE/COMMIT events advance that sidecar during the block; admission-time reporting history is instead integrity-bound into the capability.
scope_limitations: The two-block lifecycle used deterministic dependency-injected sibling interfaces and does not establish byte-level integration of all exact production V3/K-guard/atomic/attempt modules in one repository-local Python runtime.
The migrated gate was syntax-checked and exercised through its injected interfaces, but its own append/fsync/readback transition was not newly crash-injected in this run.

The historical reserved_score_pipeline_2026-08-28.py still defaults to durable_launch_capability_gate_2026-08-28.py. Injection of the new gate works at the tested contract level, but a superseding default runtime binding is still required before claiming end-to-end default-path migration.
No positive or negative conclusion extends beyond this two-block durability/replay contract.

Byte-execute the superseding path against the exact production sibling files in a repository-local runtime when available.

Add multi-process writer fencing before claiming protection against simultaneous same-slot launchers.
